name: When is it necessary to replace a bathroom countertop rather than repair it?

mainEntity.name: When is it necessary to replace a bathroom countertop rather than repair it?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should replace your countertop if you notice cracked stone, delaminating laminate, persistent water leakage around sink seals, or stubborn mold beneath an unsealed surface. Loose or deteriorating surfaces often allow water to seep into the vanity framing below, leading to concealed rot and drywall damage. Upgrading is also common when homeowners need better functionality, such as converting a single basin to a double vanity or modifying the height and clearances for disability and accessibility needs. Addressing a failing countertop early protects your cabinetry and surrounding subfloors.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace it if you see deep cracks, delamination, chronic leaks around the sink rim, or water rot that threatens the cabinet framing and subfloor beneath.
